rule_change_critical_for_pricing.summary: Gaelic football scoring changed on 1 January 2026: a kick from outside the 40-metre arc now counts TWO points.
rule_change_critical_for_pricing.detail: OLBG reports the Football Review Committee (chaired by Jim Gavin) trialled the package through 2025, that the GAA Special Congress passed all 62 recommended rule changes, and that they took permanent effect on 1 January 2026. Other changes: the 3v3 rule (three outfield players from each team in each half at all times), all kick-outs must travel beyond the 20-metre line, a solo-and-go on awarded frees, and a new advanced mark inside the 20m line. Under the 2025 trial a score from outside the arc counted only one point if an opponent touched the ball; that condition was removed for 2026.
rule_change_critical_for_pricing.scoreline_convention: A goal is still three points but the 'points' tally now blends one- and two-point scores, so a scoreline is shown as e.g. 4-18 (30) and the bracketed figure is the true total. The old shorthand no longer decomposes.
rule_change_critical_for_pricing.pricing_consequence: Match totals are structurally higher from 2026 than in earlier seasons. OLBG advises relying on 2025-onwards data rather than older seasons when assessing Total Points and handicap markets. Any Gaelic total priced from pre-2026 scoring data would be systematically too low, so pre-2026 totals are NOT used as a calibration input here.

hurling_result_of_record.statement: OLBG's Hurling hub FAQ states: 'Limerick won the 2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship, beating Galway 1-29 to 1-18 in the final at Croke Park on 19 July 2026. It was Limerick's 13th title and their first since 2023.'
hurling_result_of_record.verification_status: UNVERIFIED against the GAA. OLBG is not the governing body; the official source is gaa.ie. Left as an OLBG-reported claim and flagged rather than adopted as fact.
hurling_result_of_record.related_format_change: OLBG also states that from 2026 the hurling preliminary quarter-finals were scrapped, so Joe McDonagh Cup finalists no longer feed into the All-Ireland series at that stage.
